articles.author: Nikita
articles.description:
A teammate kept leaving reviews half done. He'd open a pull request, add a few comments and move on without clicking "Submit review". The comments sat there marked "Pending". Only he could see them. The author waited for feedback that was already written.
It's an easy mistake. GitHub saves each comment the moment you add it, so it feels like you're done. People have been asking GitHub to make this clearer since 2022.
So I built Unsubmitted Review Alert. It notices the pending review and won't let you walk away from it quietly.

The extension asks for nothing beyond github.com: no token, no network requests, no storage. So the page is the only source of truth.
The best signal on it is the counter on GitHub's "Submit review" button, because GitHub's own React state renders it:

articles.author: AI Predictions Dev
articles.description:
One of our three NVIDIA GB10 machines, the DGX Spark class of box, has switched itself off six times since July, and the system log never said why. This is how we found out what killed it each time, what the numbers looked like, and the small free tool that came out of it.
journalctl -b -1 simply ends mid-activity. There is no shutdown in it: a hard power-off never gives journald the time to write its last minutes.
last -x still lists the previous boot as still running, because nothing ever recorded its end.
The hardware watchdog did nothing. A watchdog reboots a machine that hangs; this one had no power.
After one of them, the clock came back with a date weeks in the past.
So the one question you have after the machine comes back, why did it switch off?, has no answer in the logs.
Before …
articles.title: DGX Spark thermal shutdown: how to tell whether heat switched your GB10 off

articles.author: Sahadat Husain
articles.description:
A byte budget for images is a small script that walks a folder, compares each file to a limit for its format, and exits with code 1 when any file is over. CI treats a non-zero exit as a failed check. We ran ours on a real 1,585-image folder: it flagged 24 files and the total was 85,778,075 bytes against a 12,000,000 byte budget.
Nobody reviews a binary diff. A reviewer sees "Bin 0 -> 9804300 bytes" and approves. One camera photo committed straight from a phone is 9.8 MB, and it ships to every visitor until someone notices.
A budget turns that into a failing check on the pull request. The rule is written down, so the argument happens once, in a config, not in every review.
It needs no dependencies. It walks the tree with readdir, reads each size with stat, and compares it to a limit chosen …
articles.title: Fail CI when an image is over its byte budget (Node script)

The mechanic asks when the brakes were last checked. You know it was "sometime last year". The receipt is in the glovebox, or a drawer, or gone.
That's the problem AutoLog started from. People with a car, a motorbike and a work truck, or a freelancer with one van, who keep the service history in their head and the fuel receipts in a pile. We wanted an app that answers three questions fast: what was done to this vehicle, what's due next, and what has it cost.
We also wanted it to run without a server. AutoLog has no backend, no account and no network code. Everything lives on the device in Hive CE, with Provider on top. That one constraint shaped most of the decisions below.
Service entries and fuel logs both carry an odometer reading. If users can type anything, you end up with a fill-up a…
